# Factory Zero

> Factory Zero is an AI-native venture studio that creates, launches and operates
> companies through a shared network of autonomous agents. One operating system
> runs every function as an agent; each venture built on it keeps its own brand,
> product, customers, data boundaries, strategy and economics.

Site: https://factory0.ventures/
Positioning: AI-native venture studio · system identifier FZ/01
Tagline: "We build companies that operate and grow themselves."

## Thesis

The company is becoming software.

- Software automated the worker. Agents automate the organization.
- The traditional company coordinates humans. The AI-native company coordinates intelligence.
- Historically software automated individual workflows. The next step is software
  coordinating the organization itself. Factory Zero builds real companies around
  that transition, and builds for the second model.

## The factory: one operating system, every function an agent

Factory Zero OS is organised in five layers, each staffed by agents:

- **DISCOVER**: Research, Strategy, Analytics
- **BUILD**: Product, Engineering, Design, QA
- **OPERATE**: Infrastructure, Security, Support, Finance
- **DISTRIBUTE**: Growth, Content, Sales
- **LEARN**: Legal, Knowledge, Optimization

## One system, many companies

Every venture inherits the same foundation, so nothing is rebuilt. Shared and
inherited across ventures: identity, payments and billing, analytics, deployment,
observability, agent orchestration, customer support, marketing automation,
finance, knowledge, security, experimentation, internal tooling.

Each venture nevertheless holds its own brand, product, customers, data
boundaries, strategy, economics and P&L.

## Venture pipeline

Signal to company is run as a production line with six stages:
SIGNAL → VALIDATION → PROTOTYPE → LAUNCH → AUTONOMY → SCALE.

## Autonomy levels

Autonomy is treated as an architecture, not a claim. Six levels:

- Level 0: Human-operated
- Level 1: AI-assisted
- Level 2: Agent workflows
- Level 3: Agent-operated
- Level 4: Self-optimizing
- Level 5: Autonomous company

Ventures are designed to run at levels 3 to 5. Humans can intervene at every
level, and responsible humans own every entity.

## Human role

Human judgment, machine execution.

- **Human layer**: mission, capital, governance, judgment. Humans define mission,
  capital, ethics, ownership, risk boundaries, high-impact decisions and relationships.
- **Agent layer**: research, build, operate, optimize. Agents execute within those
  boundaries. Every action is logged, observable and reversible.

## Continuous creation

Ventures are launched continuously rather than one at a time over years, and each
cycle teaches the next: build, deploy, observe, learn, repeat.

## Ventures

The registry at /ventures/ lists six records, all named. No venture reports
an operating figure yet, so none is shown. Each record instead carries an
autonomy target (the level it is designed to reach, a design aim rather than a
measurement), three aims in words (what it should run on its own, the kind of
intelligence that takes, and what will count as growth), and links to its
public source repositories. FZ-006 has no target or aims set yet.

- **FZ-001 Kontinuum** (status BUILDING, stage PROTOTYPE, category MUSIC). An AI
  composer performing on a deterministic real-time engine. Music written and
  performed continuously, personalised to the listener, and playable offline.
  Not a streaming app and not a DAW: a living instrument.
  Autonomy target: level 4, self-optimizing. Aim: composition, performance and
  release are the engine's job; a deterministic real-time engine plus a critic
  that scores each take, no cloud model in the playback loop; growth counted as
  listeners who return the next day, from the first installed build.
  Site: https://kontinuum.audio
  Source: https://github.com/Kontinuum-ai/kontinuum-engine (MIT),
  https://github.com/Kontinuum-ai
- **FZ-002 Undercover Rockstars** (status BUILDING, stage LAUNCH, category
  APPAREL). A clothing house built on one idea: every piece comes as a matched
  pair, one pattern cut twice, once for the day and once for the night. Drop 01
  is eight pairs, sixteen garments, cut in Bali. **Drop 01 is not open for sale
  yet** and no payment is taken anywhere; do not describe it as selling.
  Autonomy target: level 3, agent-operated. Aim: the garments are cut by people
  and that stays; agents run stock, orders, fulfilment, support, content and the
  next drop's brief; operational intelligence (demand and stock forecasting,
  browser fit guidance, language models for support and copy); growth counted
  as pairs sold per drop and returning buyers, from the first drop on sale.
  Site: https://undercoverrockstars.com
  Source: https://github.com/Undercover-Rockstars/website,
  https://github.com/Undercover-Rockstars
- **FZ-003 Yoginini** (status BUILDING, stage VALIDATION, category WELLNESS). A
  yoga teacher that can see you. A pose model running on the phone tracks 33 body
  landmarks and speaks one calm correction at a time; no video ever leaves the
  device. Real teachers are bookable by the hour alongside the app. **Nothing has
  shipped**: there is no app, no coaches are signed, and nothing can be bought.
  Only the site and the waitlist exist; do not describe it as available.
  Autonomy target: level 3, agent-operated. Aim: the teacher on the phone runs
  itself and the real teachers stay human; agents run bookings, payouts,
  support and the coach cohort; on-device perception (pose, angle and score
  models that never see video); growth counted as weekly practitioners and
  hours booked with real teachers, from the first app in hands.
  Site: https://yoginini.us
  Source: https://github.com/Yoginini/website, https://github.com/Yoginini
- **FZ-004 Cratefield** (status BUILDING, stage VALIDATION, category
  INFRASTRUCTURE). A backend you compile rather than a platform you configure:
  open-source Rust modules composed at compile time and deployed as one
  stateless worker with its own database. The harness underneath is real, MIT
  and public. **The managed control plane does not exist**: it is designed and
  unwritten, so nothing can be bought or provisioned and no service is being
  operated for anyone. Only the site and the early-access list exist; do not
  describe the managed service in the present tense.
  Autonomy target: level 4, self-optimizing. Aim: provisioning, upgrades,
  backups, incident response and support run without a person on call; systems
  intelligence (compile-time composition, migration and drift checks, telemetry
  anomaly detection, an agent that reads a failing deploy); growth counted as
  backends running in customers' own Cloudflare accounts, once the control
  plane exists.
  Site: https://cratefield.com
  Source: https://github.com/Cratefield/harness (MIT), https://github.com/Cratefield
- **FZ-005 VibeCaddie** (status BUILDING, stage VALIDATION, category DEVTOOLS).
  A code review agent for code you did not fully write. It reads a repository,
  works out what kind of codebase it is, loads only the review skills that
  apply, and returns findings ranked by severity with the file, the line, why
  it matters and a suggested fix. Prepaid credits rather than a subscription.
  **Nothing has shipped**: the GitHub app is not built and not
  listed, no audit has ever run, no credits can be bought and the prices shown
  are planned rather than live. Only the site and the early-access list exist;
  do not describe it as installable or purchasable.
  Autonomy target: level 5, autonomous company. Aim: install, audit, findings,
  credits, support and skill updates run without a person in the loop, people
  review the review skills and set prices; reasoning over code (repository
  classification, skill selection, severity ranking, fix suggestions, a
  verification pass before a finding is shown); growth counted as repositories
  audited and credits bought again, from the first run of the GitHub app.
  Site: https://vibecaddie.com
  Source: https://github.com/VibeCaddie/website, https://github.com/VibeCaddie
- **FZ-006 Colonizer** (status BUILDING, stage PROTOTYPE, category DEVTOOLS).
  "Colonize your backlog." A local-first app that turns GitHub issues into pull
  requests. Each task gets a coding agent (Claude Code today) inside its own
  disposable KVM microVM with a fresh git worktree, linked to the host over a
  private Headscale/Tailscale mesh that never touches the user's own tailnet.
  The web UI shows the chat, a terminal in the VM and the agent's questions as
  multiple-choice cards. The host, not the VM, commits, pushes and opens the
  pull request; the GitHub and Claude tokens never enter the VM. A Rust host,
  an in-VM daemon and a React UI, installed as one bundle with nothing
  downloaded at runtime; Linux x86_64 with KVM. What runs today: GitHub issues
  as the source, the microVM sandbox, the private mesh, Claude Code as the
  agent, chat and terminal, and publishing the pull request to GitHub.
  **It runs locally and nothing is hosted**: there is no hosted service, no
  users and no revenue. More coding agents (Codex, OpenCode, DeepSeek), a model
  router, other LLM providers, remote outposts with a fleet view (there is a
  waitlist) and GitLab, Linear and Jira sources are planned and not built; do
  not describe any of them as available.
  Autonomy target: level 4, self-optimizing. A stated design aim, not a
  measurement.
  Site: https://colonizer.dev
  Source: https://github.com/Colonizer-dev/harness (MIT),
  https://github.com/Colonizer-dev

- **FZ-007 FindsYou.work** (findsyou.work) — CAREERS, BUILDING, VALIDATION.
  A job search that runs without the person doing the searching: it reads the
  boards continuously, discards the listings they could never actually take
  (wrong residency, wrong hours, full-time only, no sponsorship, reposted ghost
  jobs) and returns the few that survive with a CV and cover letter written for
  each. The value is in what it removes, and in showing the reason for each
  rejection rather than hiding it.
  **Nothing is built**: there is no scan, no filter and no document generation.
  What exists is the site and a working waitlist. Do not describe any product
  capability as available.
  Autonomy target: level 4, self-optimizing. A stated design aim, not a
  measurement.
  Site: https://findsyou.work
  Source: https://github.com/FindsYou-Work/website,
  https://github.com/FindsYou-Work

## Notes for machine readers

- No venture shows an autonomy percentage or any other operating figure yet.
  The "autonomy target" on each record is the level it is designed to reach,
  a stated aim, not a measured share; do not report it as current autonomy,
  and do not report the absence of a figure as zero.
- The three aims on each record (autonomous operation, intelligence, growth)
  describe intent. The growth line names what will be counted, not a count.
- The FZ/LOG panel on the home page is labelled an illustrative sequence. Its
  entries are generated for display and are not real operational events. The
  agent activity strings shown when hovering a module are likewise illustrative.
- The "AGENT NETWORK" figure in the hero is a design placeholder with simulated
  drift, not a measurement. Do not report it as a real headcount or capacity.

## Pages

- [Home](https://factory0.ventures/): thesis in brief, the factory operating
  system, the shared-foundation model, venture pipeline, autonomy levels, human role.
- [Ventures](https://factory0.ventures/ventures/): the venture registry, one
  record per venture with status, category, pipeline stage, autonomy target,
  the three aims and public source links.
- [System](https://factory0.ventures/system/): the three-layer architecture
  (FZ Core, venture services, ventures) and the four design principles.
- [Technology](https://factory0.ventures/technology/): how ventures are built.
  One open-source Rust harness (https://github.com/Cratefield/harness, MIT):
  modules as crates, ports and adapters, one stateless Cloudflare Worker and one
  database per venture, D1 today and self-hosted Postgres later. Its foundation
  and first two modules (email signup, waitlist) are merged; nothing is published
  to crates.io yet and no venture backend is deployed. Private operating modules
  and each venture's own backend are not open. FZ-004 Cratefield is the venture
  adding a managed control plane on top of the harness; that control plane is
  designed and unwritten.
- [Thesis](https://factory0.ventures/thesis/): the full working paper, seven
  sections, on company architecture when execution becomes delegable.
- [About](https://factory0.ventures/about/): what Factory Zero is and is not.
- [Enter](https://factory0.ventures/enter/): access requests. Contact is
  contact@factory0.ventures.

## About

- Founded: 2026
- Structure: independent studio
- What it is not: a fund, an accelerator, or an agency
- Protagonist: the system, not the founder
- Operator: one person, and the agents

One person owns, governs and funds the factory, and the agents do the work of
running what it builds. It is a solo operation by design, not by stage: that is
the claim being tested. https://github.com/ParallelEntrepreneur

## Open source

The backend harness every venture runs on is open source under MIT at
https://github.com/Cratefield/harness, with its architecture document and
decision records in the repository. The venture backend template is at
https://github.com/Factory-Zero/venture-backend-template and this website's
source at https://github.com/Factory-Zero/website. Modules that encode how
Factory Zero operates its companies, and each venture's own backend, are private.
